evidence.summary: Painter is unstable on tier0/semantics/quantisation-thirds: its after-reopen recording r2 differs from its same-session recording r1 on 16 of the 36 maps (parity/reports/phase0/tier0-stability.md §4). Under decision 032 r1 is the exact target and every comparison against r1 must be exact; this entry covers only the comparisons against r2, per map in native units (16-bit codes of the 16-bit PNG exports, float values of the OpenEXR exports). Its bounds are the evaluator's published r2 residuals (parity/semantics/quantisation-profile.json, entry quantisation-isolated-root): max |delta| 512 codes (sRGB8, one 8-bit code), per-map mean at most 257 (L8, one 8-bit code on every texel of a map). Not covered: the RGB32F and L32F residuals against r1 (6 of 16 values off by 2^-25 or 2^-24), which stay divergences (task phase1.10_compositor-float32-residual).

evidence.summary: Painter is unstable on tier0/semantics/export-ocio-encode-legacy (the domain tier0/colour/ocio-encode; R5's Legacy twin, the only recorded golden of the domain): after save and reopen, r2 of set s5 (the 8-bit sRGB ramp at 1:1 on BaseColor inside a group masked by grey A) differs from r1 on 15 947 of 196 608 BaseColor values (14 662 texels) in each export, PNG 16 (max |delta| 619 codes, mean 20.1657), PNG 8 (max 2 codes) and OpenEXR 32f (max 0.015625), and in the two probe exports of the same map; only texels where the mask is strictly between 0 and 1 differ, and every other map of the golden is stable (parity/reports/phase0/tier0-stability.md §4). Under decision 032 r1 is the exact target and every comparison against r1 must be exact (the evaluator writes r1's three BaseColor files of s5 byte for byte, tests/export/test_export_encoders.py::test_srgb8_bitmap_equals_painter_files; decision 152); this entry covers only the comparisons against r2, per map in native units (16-bit codes, 8-bit codes, float values). Its bounds are the r2 residuals of the PNG 16 export, the largest: max |delta| 619 codes, mean 20.1657, 15 947 values differing.
